title: The Clockworks
subject: A single atmospheric scene showing three types of bronze clockwork automatons that serve as extensions of an ancient facility, all inhabiting one continuous environment. These are not creatures — they are the building's limbs. They move with mechanical precision, have too many legs, and watch with crystal lenses instead of eyes.
layout: Three groupings arranged across one continuous space, each type at a different scale, shown in their natural context within the facility. A single cohesive illustration of a living environment — not a diagram, not an annotated plate, not a labelled reference sheet.

maintenance_units.description: The smallest and most numerous. Spider-like, roughly the size of a large hand. Four to six multi-jointed bronze limbs. A central body housing one or two crystal lenses that swivel independently. They crawl across walls, ceilings, and instruments performing constant upkeep — polishing lenses, clearing dust from channels, tightening fittings.
maintenance_units.behavior: Industrious, oblivious, everywhere. They ignore people entirely unless something disrupts the facility. Show two or three of them clustered on a wall panel, mid-task.
maintenance_units.position: Upper left portion of the image. Shown on a wall or instrument surface at close range.

calibration_assistants.description: Larger — roughly the size of a cat or small dog. Six to eight limbs, some ending in gripping claws, others in flat pads for holding instruments steady. A more prominent lens array — three or four crystals arranged in a geometric cluster. They assist the facility's users by holding tools, marking measurements, and guiding positioning.
calibration_assistants.behavior: Attentive and responsive. Show one holding a crystal lens at a precise angle while another extends a measuring arm. They have a quality of alert helpfulness — like well-trained assistants anticipating the next instruction.
calibration_assistants.position: Center of the image. Shown on a workshop platform or floor, actively assisting with calibration work.

defensive_systems.description: The largest, built into walls and floors. Angular and heavy where the others are delicate. Folded flat against surfaces when dormant — easy to mistake for architectural detail. When activated, they unfold: thick bronze limbs, reinforced plating, wider lens arrays. Not built to kill — built to restrain, contain, and block.
defensive_systems.behavior: Show one mid-unfold — half-emerged from a wall recess, limbs extending, lenses brightening. The transition from architecture to automaton. A second one fully dormant in the background, flush with the wall, barely distinguishable from a decorative panel.
defensive_systems.position: Right side and lower portion of the image. One unfolding from a wall, one still dormant and camouflaged.

shared_features: Tarnished bronze construction throughout — not shiny or new, but kept functional by the smaller units
Crystal lenses instead of eyes — clear or faintly amber, mounted on swiveling joints
Too many limbs — every type has more appendages than feels comfortable
No faces, no mouths, no suggestion of personality or emotion
Joints and segments that are precise and machined, not organic
Geometric patterns etched faintly into their carapaces, matching the facility's aesthetic
mood: Clinical fascination with an undercurrent of unease. These things are useful and even elegant, but they are not friendly. They serve the building, not the people in it. The feeling of watching insects that happen to be made of bronze.
lighting: Warm amber glow from the facility's channels provides the primary light. The crystal lenses catch and refract this light — small bright points on each automaton. The dormant defensive unit sits in lower light, harder to spot.
color_palette: verdigris patina on older joints and recesses
amber light reflected in crystal lenses
dark stone and shadow of the facility walls
faint pale highlights on machined edges
composition: Arranged to show scale progression from small to large, left to right. Each type is shown in context — on a wall, on a platform, emerging from architecture — rather than floating against a blank background. The environment ties them together as parts of one system. The dormant defensive unit blending into the wall should reward a second look.
aspect_ratio: 16:9 landscape — wide enough to show all three types with breathing room

house_style_overrides.wear_note: These automatons are an exception to the default heavily-worn, mended look: the maintenance units keep all three types clean and fully functional. Render the bronze as tarnished and patina'd with age, but not rusted, broken, or damaged — no missing parts or decay. The metal stays honest worked bronze, never mirror-polished or new.

do_not_include: cute or friendly expressions — these have no expressions at all
glowing energy weapons or offensive armaments
rust, breakage, or visible decay — the maintenance units keep everything functional
organic elements — no flesh, no chitin, no biological components
steampunk aesthetic with exposed gears and pipes — this is ancient precision engineering, not Victorian industry
ANY text, labels, captions, titles, numbers, headings, or written words anywhere in the image
annotation boxes, callout lines, legends, parchment notes, or reference-sheet / diagram framing of any kind
